method: Unmodified emitted release JS. Ordered initializer stubs: core, runtime; remainder charged to app/startup. No reoptimisation. Compression interactions depend on order. Core leave-one-out is also recorded for criterion 5.

-- PREPEND IN LOOP ------------------- examples/bike-wars/src/Helpers.beni:36:35

This puts elements in front of `acc`, the accumulator this `List.foldr` hands
back to its callback, so it happens at every step:

    [ (…), …acc ]

A list is an array, so every step copies the whole accumulator, and the loop
takes time that grows with the square of the list's length. Add at the end
instead, which takes the same short time at every step:

    [ …acc, (…) ]

`List.foldr` hands over the last element first, so to keep the order write
the loop as `List.foldl`, which hands over the first element first.

If the prepend is meant — the list stays short — give the new list a name
first, and this warning goes.

36|                [ [ start, end ], …acc ]
                                     ^^^^

-- PREPEND IN LOOP ------------------- examples/bike-wars/src/Helpers.beni:51:39

This puts elements in front of `acc`, which this function hands back to
itself, so it happens at every step of a loop:

    [ (…), …acc ]

A list is an array, so every step copies the whole accumulator, and the loop
takes time that grows with the square of the list's length. Add at the end
instead, which takes the same short time at every step:

    [ …acc, (…) ]

That keeps the elements in the order they arrive, so the `List.reverse` that
put a prepended result back in order is no longer needed.

If the prepend is meant — the list stays short — give the new list a name
first, and this warning goes.

                                         ^^^^
